title: Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture on adding matching components
statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $K_2$ denote the complete graph on two vertices. A pair $(G,H)$ is **Ramsey-finite** if it has only finitely many Ramsey-minimal graphs. **Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture.** If $(G,H)$ is Ramsey-finite, then $(G\cup \ell K_2,H\cup mK_2)$ is Ramsey-finite for all integers $\ell,m\ge 0$. This conjecture concerns the stability of Ramsey-finiteness under adjoining arbitrary numbers of isolated matching components to the two target graphs. The paper states that this conjecture is true.
source_name: Yaping Mao, “Ramsey-finiteness for graph pairs: A complete solution to the Burr-Erdős-Faudree-Schelp conjectures”, arXiv:2604.17356 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17356

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of April 2026). “The two 1981 conjectures are true, whereas Burr's stronger survey conjecture is false.”
